title: Leave and Holiday Policy
sections: Purpose and Scope
This policy outlines the terms and conditions for leave and holiday entitlement for shore-based employees of Calder Bay Ship Management Ltd.
It is designed to ensure fair and consistent treatment of all eligible employees in accordance with company standards.
Shore-based employees include all individuals employed in administrative, operational, technical, and support roles within the company's headquarters and regional offices.
These roles are defined in the company's employment classification system.
Employees working onshore are entitled to leave and holiday benefits as outlined in this policy, which is distinct from the terms applicable to seafarers covered under separate crew agreements.
The policy does not extend to individuals employed under contract, temporary, or part-time arrangements unless explicitly stated in their respective employment agreements.
The policy applies to all employees who are currently in active employment with Calder Bay Ship Management Ltd and who are classified as shore-based under the company's internal records.
Annual Leave Entitlement
Full-time shore employees are entitled to 24 working days of annual leave per calendar year. This entitlement accrues at a rate of 2 working days per month.
Leave accrual is automatically tracked by the human resources department and recorded in the employee's personal leave account. This account is updated monthly in accordance with the accrual rate.

Leave may be taken in one continuous block or in multiple blocks, provided that the total number of working days does not exceed the annual entitlement. Any unused leave may be carried forward to the next calendar year.
The annual leave entitlement is subject to the terms of the employee's employment contract and any applicable company policies.
Carrying Leave Over
Unused annual leave may be carried over to the next year, subject to the limits outlined in this section. Up to 5 working days of unused annual leave can be carried over and expire on 31 March.

Employees must submit a written request to their line manager by 31 January to carry over unused annual leave. The request should include the number of days they wish to carry over and the reason for the carry-over.
If approved, the carried-over leave will be added to the employee’s annual leave entitlement for the following year. The leave must be taken within the period specified in the leave schedule.
Any unused carry-over leave not taken by 31 March will be forfeited and cannot be reclaimed in subsequent years. This applies to all employees regardless of tenure or position.
Employees are advised to consult their line manager early to ensure compliance with this policy and to avoid the loss of accrued leave.
Requesting Leave

All leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal to ensure proper record-keeping and timely processing. Employees are required to provide sufficient details about the dates and nature of the leave to facilitate manager review.
Annual leave requests need 10 working days notice to allow adequate planning. Managers are expected to respond within 3 working days to confirm or deny the request.
Requests for leave should include the start and end dates, along with a brief explanation of the reason for the absence. This information helps in assessing the impact on team operations.
Managers are responsible for reviewing leave requests and providing feedback through the HR portal. They must ensure all responses are clear and communicated promptly.
Leave requests that do not meet the required notice period may be denied without further action. Employees are encouraged to plan ahead to avoid disruptions to their work schedule.
Employees are advised to consult with their manager before submitting a leave request to discuss any potential impacts on their responsibilities.
Sick Leave
Employees are entitled to 12 working days of paid sick leave per calendar year. A medical certificate is required after 2 consecutive working days of absence.
Sick leave must be reported to the manager before the start of the working day. Failure to report in a timely manner may result in the leave being considered unauthorized.
Employees are responsible for providing a medical certificate to their manager upon returning to work. The certificate must confirm the nature and duration of the illness.
Leave due to illness must be recorded in the employee's personal leave record. This record is maintained by the human resources department.
Employees are required to notify their manager of any anticipated absence due to illness. This notification should include the expected duration of the leave.
Medical certificates must be submitted in the original format and cannot be copied or faxed. The certificate must include the employee's full name and details of the illness.
Public Holidays

The shore office observes 12 public holidays per year, which are defined in the official calendar maintained by the human resources department. Public holidays that fall within a period of annual leave are not counted as leave days.

Employees are responsible for checking the official calendar for public holiday dates and ensuring their leave requests do not overlap with scheduled work travel. Any travel on a public holiday is covered by the Travel and Expense Policy and may be compensated with time off in lieu.

In the event of a public holiday falling on a weekend, the holiday is observed on the following weekday unless otherwise specified in the official calendar. Employees must confirm their availability for any work required on such days.

All public holidays are considered non-working days for the shore office, and any work performed on these days is subject to the terms outlined in the Travel and Expense Policy and the relevant operational guidelines.
Parental Leave
Eligible employees are entitled to 16 weeks of paid maternity leave and 2 weeks of paid paternity leave following the birth of a child.
The maternity leave period begins on the first day following the child's birth and is intended to allow the employee to recover and bond with the newborn.
The paternity leave period starts on the first day following the child's birth and is intended to allow the employee to support the family during the early stages of the child's life.
During the leave period, the employee's position will be held open, and all benefits will be maintained in accordance with company policy.
Upon return to work, the employee will be expected to resume their duties as agreed with their line manager, with no expectation of reduced hours unless mutually agreed.
Compassionate Leave
Employees are entitled to compassionate leave following the death of an immediate family member. Compassionate leave is 5 working days.

This documentation must be submitted in the original form or an official certified copy. During the compassionate leave period, the employee is expected to maintain contact with their line manager to discuss any necessary arrangements for their absence.

This includes providing updates on personal circumstances and any support needs. The employee is responsible for ensuring that all work-related responsibilities are transferred to a colleague or team member before the leave begins.

This transfer should be completed within 5 working days prior to the leave start date. The line manager is responsible for approving the compassionate leave request and ensuring that all necessary arrangements are made for the employee's absence.
This includes coordinating with the HR department if required. Employees are encouraged to seek support from the company's employee assistance program during this time.
The HR department will provide details on how to access this support upon request.
Records and Queries
Leave balances are accessible through the HR portal for all employees, providing real-time visibility of accrued and remaining leave days.
Employees may submit leave-related queries via the HR portal, ensuring all requests are documented and tracked within the system.
All leave-related data, including balances and query responses, is stored securely within the HR portal and is accessible only to authorized personnel.
Employees are required to log in to the HR portal using their assigned credentials to view leave balances and submit queries.
The HR team will provide clarification or resolution to any leave-related questions raised through the portal, ensuring timely and accurate support.
